I’m 45, been farming these 20 mu for 25 years since I finished primary school. My husband works at a factory in the county seat and my daughter is at university, so most days it’s just me and my mother-in-law in the fields. My son helps on weekends but he’s in middle school. We grow wheat and maize on the same 20 mu, one after the other — it’s a busy year.

I’ll sow winter wheat around October 8, after the National Day holiday. I bought 40 jin of improved wheat seed from Old Wang’s shop, about 60 yuan per mu. I save some seed every year but I mix in new seed every three years so it stays strong. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind — before planting, and I add a small scoop of urea in the furrow too. At jointing in late March, I spread about 20 jin of urea per mu, and if the wheat looks yellow at flowering I’ll give it another 10 jin. The extension agent says 15 kg nitrogen is enough, but my neighbor Aunt Li cut back last year and her wheat was thin, only 380 jin per mu. I’m not taking that risk with my daughter’s tuition due in the fall. I’ll irrigate three times for wheat — after planting if it’s dry, at jointing, and at grain filling. Pumping costs about 30 yuan each time per mu, but dry wheat means empty grain, so I’ll pay it.

Wheat harvest is around June 10. That week is hell — we have maybe five days to get the wheat off and the maize in. I hire two or three villagers for 150 yuan a day plus lunch, and I pay a tractor driver for quick rotary tillage. If the weather turns bad we plant no-till, but I prefer to turn the soil. For maize I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 jin per mu, 80 yuan. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 40 kg per mu, and at the big trumpet stage in late July I topdress with about 20 kg urea per mu. I’ll irrigate maize twice if the summer is dry, but if the rains come I might skip one. I spray herbicide on both crops, and I watch for aphids on wheat and stem borers on maize.

I expect about 450 kg per mu for wheat and 500 kg per mu for maize in a normal year. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and water than risk a bad yield — we need cash in hand and I can’t afford a failure. All together I’m looking at about 17,000 yuan for inputs this year, which is most of our savings, but there’s no other way.
